newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH MARKETS UNMOVED BY PARLY EMU DEBATE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH MARKETS UNMOVED BY PARLY EMU DEBATE.

text.p: Finland's financial markets watched the first day of parliamentary debate on Tuesday on a government report on EMU but found no reason to care, analysts said on Wednesday.

A narrowing of the 10-year yield premium over Bunds which started on Tuesday was not connected to any belief that Finnish MPs had turned more pro-EMU -- markets have long been convinced that Finland will join in the first group, they said.
"There were no surprises. The markets don't seem to care," said chief economist Petteri Hirvonen at brokerage Protos.
A senior forex dealer called the legislature's EMU debate -- live on television on Tuesday -- "irrelevant".

Merita Bank economist Sirpa Wallius said the domestic EMU debate was not yet one "to cause any hearts to race". But markets might turn more sensitive to the tone of speeches in the autumn as the EMU vote is drawing closer, she said.

The ongoing debate will not lead to a vote on EMU membership, but may shed some light on how MPs feel about the coalition government's outspoken support for Finnish participation in the single currency from day one.
The vote on membership is scheduled for early 1998.

On Tuesday, MPs of Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's social democrats, the Leftist Alliance and the Green Party took a quite cautious view. Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto's Conservative Party came out clearly in favour while the biggest opposition group, the Centre Party, was against membership, as expected.
"The debate offered no surprises. The strong consensus view that Finland will be in the first group in EMU only strengthened," said a senior analyst, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The debate is scheduled to be completed this week. On Wednesday afternoon, were 40 MPs still waiting for their turn to speak.
After the debate, the government's EMU report will go to various of the legislature's committees.
The most keenly watched opinion on the report will be the constitutional committee's statement, which will rule by which kind of majority parliament shall vote on EMU membership.
